key_insight: EmbodiedRSI makes robot learning more adaptive by actively choosing which code and skill changes to test, instead of wasting robot trials on unguided self-improvement. It uses hypothesis-guided co-evolution to update both the robot’s behavior and the harness that guides learning.
problem_solved: The paper addresses the brittleness of robot foundation models when object positions or task instructions change, and the high cost of improving them through large-scale post-training data collection. It also tackles the inefficiency of current self-evolving systems that spend robot trials poorly when exploring new code and skill updates.
method: Uses a self-evolving framework that iteratively improves robot control performance through active continual learning.
Introduces hypothesis-guided co-evolution to prioritize promising code and skill modifications before spending real robot trials.
Reduces wasted experimentation by selecting adaptation steps based on expected utility rather than brute-force trial-and-error.
impact: For practitioners, EmbodiedRSI offers a more sample-efficient path to continual robot adaptation in changing environments. This could lower the cost of deploying robot foundation models in real-world settings where tasks and object layouts frequently shift.
